shared_elements: frontal anthropomorphic figure carved in relief on an upright monolith
elaborate headdress/headgear filling the upper zone
arms/hands rendered across the chest area
chest ornament or medallion (disc in A, pectoral-like elements in B)
carved bands or registers of small motifs on the body/surface
figure occupying the full height of a vertical stone face
justification: Both depict a single frontal anthropomorphic personage carved in relief over the whole face of an upright monolith, with a broad headdress at the top, arms folded across the chest and an ornament/medallion at the breast, which is a reasonably specific shared scheme. They differ strongly in manner and density: A is a massive, rounded, highly schematic low-relief with a few isolated motifs and plain expanses, while B is a flat slab covered edge-to-edge with fine, intricate high relief including long vertical columns of repeated square sign-blocks that have no counterpart in A.
